hero.subtitle: Straight answers about what Melusina is, who it's for, how it works, and how to get started.

faqs.question: Where does our data actually live?
faqs.answer: On your hardware. Every document, spreadsheet, chat, and photo runs in its own isolated container with its own storage. Not in Google's cloud. Not on Amazon's servers. On a machine you control.

faqs.question: Can non-technical people manage workflows?
faqs.answer: Yes. Workflows, policies, and automation rules are JSON-driven with visual editors. No redeployment needed to make changes. Admin NFTs control who can modify what.

faqs.question: What happens when information doesn't match?
faqs.answer: OCR and AI flag field-level mismatches, show the original and corrected values, and log every decision in the case timeline for auditors.

faqs.question: How do we customize the onboarding flow?
faqs.answer: Visual drag-and-drop builders. Branch by jurisdiction. Publish without waiting for engineering.

faqs.question: Can we bring our own AI models?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Deploy your own LLMs inside isolated Pearls—they never see the network. Document processing, translation, and risk scoring stay inside your perimeter with Solana Memo audit trail.

faqs.question: How does wallet login work?
faqs.answer: Three options, whichever works for your device: (1) Browser wallet extension like Phantom or Solflare, (2) Phone wallet app for Android, (3) QR code for iOS or devices without a wallet. You sign a challenge to prove you own the wallet — no passwords needed. Keyholder NFT holders get admin access automatically.

faqs.question: What screening providers are supported?
faqs.answer: Major sanctions lists (OFAC, EU, UN), PEP databases, and adverse media. Add custom sources via HTTP connectors.

faqs.question: How long until we're live?
faqs.answer: Most deployments: 2-3 weeks. Week 1: License NFT and trust chain setup. Week 2: keyholder configuration, DNS records, and vault. Week 3: pilot apps and verification.

faqs.question: Do we need dedicated infrastructure?
faqs.answer: Three options: deploy on existing cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure), install on your own hardware, or use Melusina's managed cloud. Families and small teams often start with a single machine or the managed cloud. Larger organizations typically self-host.

faqs.question: What about GDPR and data residency?
faqs.answer: You control where data lives — deploy to whatever jurisdiction you need. Container isolation guarantees no cross-tenant data mixing. Regulators can verify your license on Solana and check your DNS records independently.

faqs.question: Can we white-label the interface?
faqs.answer: Yes. Customize branding, copy, and styling through configuration. No code changes needed for visual customization.

faqs.question: How do we handle multi-language support?
faqs.answer: Built-in translation for forms and documents. AI helpers can translate and summarize in 40+ languages while preserving original artifacts.

faqs.question: What happens if a reviewer makes a mistake?
faqs.answer: All decisions are logged on the case timeline with user ID, timestamp, and justification. Admins can override with audit trail preservation.

faqs.question: Can we integrate with our CRM?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use HTTP helpers with allowlists and signed receipts. Direct database access available for custom integrations.

faqs.question: How do we handle high-risk cases?
faqs.answer: Automated rules escalate based on risk score, screening hits, or manual flags. Cases route to specialized reviewers with enhanced permissions.

faqs.question: What if we lose everything?
faqs.answer: Backups are encrypted and split among your keyholders. You need enough keyholders (e.g., 2 of 4) plus the encrypted backup to rebuild. License is on the blockchain. Keys are derived, not stored. Provision new hardware, keyholders decrypt the backup, restore, done.

faqs.question: Can we get SOC 2 certified?
faqs.answer: Melusina provides verifiable infrastructure with on-chain audit trails, threshold key management, and Pearl isolation. Your deployment and operational practices determine certification eligibility—Melusina gives auditors cryptographic proof of controls.

faqs.question: How do updates work?
faqs.answer: Updates are Foundation-signed releases with verified hashes. Your License NFT entitles you to updates. The 4-phase boot process verifies release authenticity before each startup—tampered binaries won't boot.

faqs.question: What training is included?
faqs.answer: Initial deployment includes knowledge transfer: operations training, admin workshops, and reviewer onboarding. Ongoing support available via VIP packages.

faqs.question: Can we run a pilot first?
faqs.answer: Yes. Deploy a test environment with sample cases before going live. Pilot typically runs 2-4 weeks with your team.

faqs.question: How does per-app billing work?
faqs.answer: Each container has its own SOL wallet. When it uses platform services — sending an OTP, delivering an email, running AI — a micropayment is deducted. Operators set spending limits. If the wallet runs out, the container can still run but can't use paid services until topped up.

faqs.question: How does OTP work? Do apps see the codes?
faqs.answer: No. The app never sees the OTP code. The platform generates the code, sends it to the user, and the app only gets back a cryptographic proof that the user entered it correctly. Rate-limited, timing-safe, one system for the entire platform.

faqs.question: What is a grain wallet?
faqs.answer: Every Pearl on the managed cloud has a grain wallet—a SOL escrow account tied to that specific grain. The wallet funds consumption of shared platform services: each OTP sent, each email delivered, each AI inference run deducts a micropayment. Operators preauthorize spend amounts and set hard limits. When the escrow is empty, the Pearl can still run but can't consume paid shared services until refunded. All transactions are traceable on Solana.

faqs.question: Does Melusina support push notifications?
faqs.answer: Yes. Melusina runs on your server and you access it through any browser. Push notifications are content-free by design — payloads are deliberately empty ('something happened'), preventing data from leaking through the push service. Pushes are smart: they only fire when you don't have an active connection, so you never get duplicates.

faqs.question: How do grain links (capability URLs) work?
faqs.answer: Grain links are capability URLs that carry access rights to a specific Pearl. Four modes are available: Burn-after-reading (consumed when the tab closes), Timed (expires at a specific datetime), Use-count (atomic counter—each access decrements it), and Unlimited (valid until manually revoked). For NFT-backed grains, the URL token's SHA-256 hash is stored on-chain via a Solana PDA, enabling verifiable link provenance.

faqs.question: Can one Pearl create another Pearl automatically?
faqs.answer: Yes, via the Cap'n Proto createGrain RPC—but only when admin policy rules whitelist the exact (triggerApp, targetApp) pair. The requesting Pearl must supply a context message (min 25 characters) explaining why. The user sees an approval popup before anything happens. On approval, a share-back link is returned at the configured role level. No app can silently spawn instances.

faqs.question: What makes apps talk to each other?
faqs.answer: Apps communicate using Cap'n Proto — a type-safe protocol designed by the creator of Protocol Buffers (Kenton Varda, ex-Google). No data format bugs. No serialization overhead. Apps in any language can participate with full type safety.

faqs.question: What runs alongside the core platform?
faqs.answer: Three dedicated services: an email gateway with automatic failover and DKIM signing, a Solana proxy that rate-limits and filters blockchain calls, and a clustering engine for multi-machine setups. All communicate over encrypted internal channels.

faqs.question: Does Melusina work on my phone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Melusina runs on your server or PC and you open it in any browser — laptop, phone, tablet. Add it to your home screen for one-tap access. No App Store. No Google Play. No gatekeeper. Push notifications are content-free by design — payloads carry no data.

faqs.question: What apps are already available?
faqs.answer: A growing library of production apps ships today. Highlights include Bureau (spreadsheets, documents, diagrams, image editor with real-time collaboration), CoinFace (KYC/KYB identity verification with AI-powered document extraction and facial matching), AI Lagoon (private AI hub connecting to Ollama, ChatGPT, and OpenRouter), MerMail (email + workflow management with multi-grain coordination), BotMother (Telegram bot management with auto-reply engines and ticket systems), MiniGit (Git hosting with static site publishing), and Shell Tester (developer tools). All are real codebases in Go, TypeScript, and Python — and the catalog keeps expanding.

faqs.question: What is Grapple?
faqs.answer: Grapple is how Pearls connect to each other. When a Pearl needs something — AI, payment, email, another Pearl's data — it sends a request through Grapple. You see a picker with your options and choose which specific Pearl to connect. The connection is between two specific instances, not blanket app-to-app. Revoke anytime with one click. AI Lagoon uses Grapple to offer three AI capability types (text, vision, generic) to any Pearl on the server.

faqs.question: Can I run my entire company inside Melusina?
faqs.answer: Yes — that's the point. Bureau for docs, spreadsheets, and diagrams. MerMail for email and client workflows. MiniGit for code hosting. AI Lagoon for private AI. BotMother for customer-facing Telegram bots. CoinFace for client KYC. Each is a Pearl — isolated, connected via Grapple. Build client portals by clicking Grapple and picking Pearls. Your startup doesn't use Melusina. Your startup IS Melusina.

faqs.question: How do I build a workflow without coding?
faqs.answer: Drag process steps into a pipeline: terms acceptance → contact verification → document upload → personal details → review → approval. Each step is configurable — conditional fields, jurisdiction branching, risk scoring, SLA timers. Each process runs in its own Pearl. Each respondent gets their own isolated Pearl. The admin reviews from a Station Pearl. Three-grain architecture: Station defines, Process executes, Client portal collects.
